findings.evidence: for the canonical dense 70B (80 layers, hidden 8192, full MHA — Ch 7) and for the ~47B challenger’s own attention shape (32 layers, hidden 4096, GQA with 8 KV-heads × 128 — the latter shape is the published first-party config of the Mixtral 8x7B-class model)
findings.issue: The text attributes the 32L/4096H GQA shape to the 'published first-party config of the Mixtral 8x7B-class model' but the surrounding discussion treats the model as an illustrative MoE challenger with component-derived parameters. The phrasing overstates first-party provenance for the derived decomposition.
findings.fix_instruction: Separate the two claims: the attention shape is [1P][FACT] from the published config; the parameter split and active-count arithmetic are [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]. Do not call the whole challenger a published first-party config.

findings.evidence: §3.1.1 orientation box: "It is the book's coverage of the 2026 alternative-inference frontier; the core dense/MoE/KV thread resumes in §3.2 (Mental Model). Read now for the frontier signal, or skip to §3.2 and return through the cross-references in Appendix A §9A." The text also says (page 59): "§2.1.2 (latent video) and §3.1.1 (diffusion/LLaDA-style) carry the extension." And (page 61): "read the two as one treatment."
findings.issue: The orientation box on page 60 tells the reader that §2.1.2 and §3.1.1 should be read 'as one treatment' — but §2.1.2 (page 59–60) covers whole-clip latent *video* generation (Wan2.2) while §3.1.1 (page 61) covers *diffusion/LLaDA-style* language generation. These are two different alternative-inference mechanisms with different execution schedules, not one treatment. The cross-reference on page 11 (line '(§2.1.2; §3.1.1 and Appendix A §9A)') lumps them together as if they are the same subject. A reader expecting 'one treatment' will find two distinctly scoped sub-sections.
findings.fix_instruction: Change 'read the two as one treatment' to 'read the two as a paired treatment of non-autoregressive and whole-clip generation respectively, together with Appendix A §9A' — or remove the 'one treatment' claim and list them as complementary rather than identical.

findings.evidence: "We contrast with a representative MoE model in the Mixtral lineage. Its published model card gives 46.7B total and 12.9B active parameters per token [1P][FACT]." (no model name, URL, revision or access date); "the challenger's attention geometry is [1P][FACT] … the published first-party config of the Mixtral 8x7B-class model" (p. 66); Table 5-2 (p. 123): "9,200 × 0.33 MB; 80 layers × 8 KV heads × head_dim 128 at FP16 (327,680 B/token) [1P][DERIVED]" for "Llama-2/3 70B" and "model card huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2 [1P][FACT]" (bare hostname, no scheme); Ch 7 (p. 158): "LLaMA-2 70B, for instance, has 64 query heads but only 8 KV-heads" (uncited). Preface (p. 21): "each is cited with a stable identifier in the References chapter".
findings.issue: Multiple load-bearing [1P] claims have no named, resolvable first-party source: the Mixtral-class model card is never identified (no repo, revision, or access date), the Llama-2/3 70B GQA-8 geometry that drives the ~0.33 MB/token constant and Ch 7's sensitivity note carries no citation, and the one URL given is scheme-less. This fails the book's own stable-identifier requirement and makes the [1P] tags unverifiable.
findings.fix_instruction: Name each source with a full URL plus revision/access date (e.g., the specific Mixtral model card commit, the Llama-2/Llama-3 70B config.json), add them to the References/First-hand Sources list, and add the 'https://' scheme to the mpnet model-card URL.

findings.evidence: "Because a dense model with full multi-head attention gives the cleanest single-constant KV formula (2 × layers × hidden × bytes) and the largest KV footprint — the conservative worst case an architect should always size against first." vs Ch 7 (p. 172): "a model with 100 layers and 12288 dim will have ~4.9 MB/token (2 × 100 × 12288 × 2 B = 4,915,200 B)".
findings.issue: 'The conservative worst case an architect should always size against first' is stated as an absolute, but full-MHA 70B is the worst case only within the canonical 80-layer/8192-hidden geometry; the book itself prints larger per-token KV constants for other geometries (e.g., ~4.9 MB/token). The unscoped superlative could license under-sizing against a bigger-geometry model.
findings.fix_instruction: Scope the claim: 'the largest KV footprint for a given layer count and hidden width — the conservative worst case within the canonical 80-layer/8192-hidden geometry', and cross-reference §7.4's re-derivation examples.
